question_text: Thinking is like a game, it does not begin unless there is an opposite team.
customKeyPointers: A thought that meets no resistance is only a habit
The opposite team is an argument, a person, or one's own doubt
A quarrel is not yet thinking

points.text: Thinking starts when something pushes back. Until then one is only repeating.
A scientist needs a rival hypothesis. A court needs a defence. A person needs the objection he would rather not hear.
The opposite team is not required to be hated. It is required to be real, and to be allowed to score.
A public life that silences the other side does not win the game. It cancels it, and calls the silence a conclusion.
The limit is that opposition for its own sake is only noise. The game has a point: a better account of the matter.
Thought is a team sport played against a resistance. Without the other side, nothing has begun.

question_text: Visionary decision-making happens at the intersection of intuition and logic.
customKeyPointers: Intuition sees the end before the steps are written
Logic tests whether the end can be reached
A vision that skips the test is a wish
A logic with no vision only administers the present

points.text: A visionary decision is not a feeling and it is not a spreadsheet. It is the point where the two agree.
Intuition arrives first, as a sense of what the situation is asking. It is trained by experience, and it is also capable of being a bias.
Logic asks for the evidence, the cost and the step that would prove the hunch wrong. That is how a vision becomes a decision.
A leader who will not hear the number wastes the people who must carry the vision. A system that will not hear the hunch never leaves the last successful year.
The intersection is uncomfortable, because one of the two usually has to give way.
Visionary decisions are rare because most people stay on one road: the feeling, or the file.

question_text: Not all who wander are lost.
customKeyPointers: Lost means without a direction. Wandering can be a way of finding one
A fixed path is not the only proof of purpose
The line does not defend a drift that refuses every arrival

points.text: To wander is to move without the final map. To be lost is not to know why one is moving.
A scientist, a pilgrim and a young person changing work are all wanderers whom a timetable would call aimless.
The search is the purpose. A society that honours only the straight career will call that search a failure.
The charity of the line has a limit. Wandering that learns nothing, and will not stop, is a loss with a romantic name.
The distinction is whether the person can say, even roughly, what he is looking for.
Not all who wander are lost. Some are lost and walking, and the sentence was never meant to hide them.

question_text: Inspiration for creativity springs from the effort to look for the magical in the mundane.
customKeyPointers: Creativity is a way of looking, before it is a talent
The mundane is where most of life actually happens
Waiting for a grand subject is how most work never starts

points.text: The sentence locates inspiration not in a rare event but in a second look at an ordinary one.
A kitchen, a bus queue, a failure of a machine: these are mundane, and they are also where a poem, a design or a scientific question usually begins.
The effort is the point. The magical does not announce itself. Someone has to refuse to find the ordinary boring.
This is as true of a laboratory as of a studio. A careful attention to a dull result has started more discoveries than a hunt for the sublime.
The risk is to decorate the mundane and call it magic. The real effort changes what one is able to notice.
Inspiration springs from attention. The mundane is simply the place attention is most often absent.

question_text: Girls are weighed down by restrictions, boys with demands – two equally harmful disciplines.
customKeyPointers: One gender is told not to go. The other is told not to fail
Both are disciplines, and both shrink a person
The harms are equal in kind and not always equal in consequence

points.text: The sentence pairs two trainings that look different and damage in the same way: each refuses the child a full life.
A girl is weighed down by a restriction on movement, dress, study and desire. The discipline says her safety is her smallness.
A boy is weighed down by a demand to earn, to be hard, and never to need help. The discipline says his worth is his usefulness.
They are equal as harms to freedom. They are not equal as exposure to violence, which still falls more heavily on the restricted girl.
A reform that frees only one side leaves the other as the enforcer of the old rule.
Two disciplines, one purpose: a smaller human being. Ending either requires ending both.

question_text: Mathematics is the music of reason.
customKeyPointers: Music is pattern heard. Mathematics is pattern proved
Reason without form is opinion
The line praises a beauty that is also binding

points.text: The sentence calls mathematics a music because it is a pattern that satisfies, and a music of reason because the pattern has to be true.
A proof, like a melody, is a sequence in which each step is compelled by the one before it.
That compulsion is why mathematics can describe a planet, a price and a bridge. The beauty is not a decoration. It is the sign that the relation is tight.
Reason that will not submit to this discipline remains a preference. Number is how a preference is made to face a check.
The analogy has a limit. Music may move a person who does not understand it. A theorem that is not understood has not yet been heard.
Mathematics is the music of reason because it is the only music in which being moved and being right are the same event.

question_text: A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity.
customKeyPointers: Charity gives back a little of what injustice took
Justice changes the rule so that the taking does not happen
Charity remains for the misfortune that no rule can prevent

points.text: Charity treats a wound. Justice asks why the wound keeps being made.
A wage that cannot buy food, a school that was never built, a title to land that was taken: each produces a person who then needs a donation.
A just rule — a fair wage, a public school, a secure right — retires that donation. The need shrinks because the cause was removed.
Charity can even delay justice, if the giver enjoys the role and the receiver is trained to be grateful instead of entitled.
Some needs remain: an illness, a disaster, a person no institution has yet imagined. Charity is the right answer there, and only there.
More justice, less charity. The charity that survives is the kind a just society still has occasions for.

question_text: Education is what remains after one has forgotten what one has learned in school.
customKeyPointers: The syllabus fades. A habit of mind can remain
What remains is curiosity, a standard, and the ability to learn again
The line is not an excuse for refusing to learn the facts

points.text: The sentence separates a stock of lessons, which is forgotten, from an education, which is the person those lessons left behind.
Dates, formulae and a definition go. What can remain is the habit of asking for a reason, of reading a page, and of not being fooled by a confident speaker.
A school that drills only the recallable item produces a result and, years later, an empty cupboard.
The sentence is often misused to despise knowledge. One cannot forget what was never learned, and the remainder is made out of what was once known.
The test of a school is the adult who no longer remembers the chapter and can still think.
Education is the residue: a mind that kept its shape after the syllabus fell away.
